use.how: Xは(私には)高嶺の花だ. Said of something or someone you admire and want but cannot hope to get: a luxury item, a home, a person you have a crush on.

cue: Every day on your way home you stare at a luxury watch in a shop window, knowing you will never be able to afford it.

ctx.s: あのブランドのバッグは、私[わたし]には{高嶺[たかね]の花[はな]}だ。
ctx.en: That designer bag is way out of my reach.

ctx.s: 「都心[としん]のマンションなんて、{高嶺[たかね]の花[はな]}だよ。」
ctx.en: "A flat in central Tokyo? That's just a dream."

ctx.s: クラスで一番[いちばん]人気[にんき]の彼女[かのじょ]は、僕[ぼく]にとって{高嶺[たかね]の花[はな]}だった。
ctx.en: The most popular girl in class was completely out of my league.

ctx.s: 一度[いちど]は乗[の]ってみたいけれど、ファーストクラスは{高嶺[たかね]の花[はな]}だ。
ctx.en: I'd love to fly first class once, but it's far beyond my means.

ctx.s: かつては{高嶺[たかね]の花[はな]}だった海外旅行[かいがいりょこう]も、今[いま]では身近[みぢか]になった。
ctx.en: Travelling abroad, once out of reach for most people, is now commonplace.

ctx.s: 社内[しゃない]の{高嶺[たかね]の花[はな]}と言[い]われていた先輩[せんぱい]が、結婚[けっこん]を発表[はっぴょう]した。
ctx.en: The colleague everyone at work considered out of their league announced her marriage.

bad.s: やっと買[か]った新車[しんしゃ]は、私[わたし]の{高嶺[たかね]の花[はな]}だ。
bad.en: (meant: the new car I finally bought is my pride and joy)
bad.why: It is something out of reach; once you own it, it no longer is. A car you are proud of is jiman no kuruma.

bad.s: この数学[すうがく]の問題[もんだい]は難[むずか]しすぎて、{高嶺[たかね]の花[はな]}だ。
bad.en: (meant: this maths problem is too hard for me to solve)
bad.why: It is for something you desire and admire, not a task that is too hard. A problem beyond you is te ni oenai.
